# A Rich and Active Commerce Between Thoughts and Experiences

Pragmatism[^1] only follows[^2] the example of the sister-sciences, interpreting the unobserved by the observed.[^3] It brings old and new harmoniously together.[^4] It converts the absolutely empty notion of a static relation of 'correspondence'[^5] between our minds and reality, into that of a rich and active commerce (that anyone may follow in detail and understand) between particular thoughts of ours, and the great universe of other experiences in which they play their parts and have their uses.[^6]

[^1]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "Pragmatism"
[^2]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "only follows"
[^3]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "the example of the sister-sciences, interpreting the unobserved by the observed."
[^4]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "It brings old and new harmoniously together."
[^5]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "It converts the absolutely empty notion of a static relation of 'correspondence'"
[^6]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Rationalistic Criticisms]] "between our minds and reality, into that of a rich and active commerce (that anyone may follow in detail and understand) between particular thoughts of ours, and the great universe of other experiences in which they play their parts and have their uses."
